content.text:
Activation emails should work again. The fix is live on production and staging, and committed as `40041d2` (pushed to Entire and GitHub).

**The cause:** the mailbox password in `.env` was changed on 25 October, but the PHP-FPM worker processes serving the website had been running since 24 October. `Email.php` read the password with `getenv()`, which returns what's in the worker process's own memory. CodeIgniter's `.env` loader never overwrites a variable a process already holds, so those workers kept sending the old password. Production's cached copy was 17 characters against 14 in `.env`. Command-line tests always start a fresh process, which is why they worked.

**The fix:**
1. `app/Config/Email.php` now reads the password with CodeIgniter's `env()`, which takes this request's value from `.env`, so a future password change can't go stale. The old file is backed up in `/root/skiv2-email-backup-1793136695` and `/root/skiv2-staging-email-backup-1793136695` on the VPS.
2. I gracefully reloaded PHP-FPM, so all its workers are fresh, and cleared both sites' caches. My first reload signal went to the container's process supervisor by mistake (it only reopened log files, no effect on the site); the second went to PHP-FPM correctly.

**Checked:**
- **Staging:** a fresh test sign-up logged in to Hostinger successfully (the email only bounced because example.test addresses can't receive mail), and the cached password now matches `.env`.
- **Production:** it's up. The last login failure was at 23:22:45, before the reload.

**Not confirmed yet:** a real activation email on production. I didn't create a production account to test. The next real sign-up will show it, and I can check the log for you.

**Still to do on your side:**
- **Change the mailbox password.** It's exposed in this session from my earlier mistake. After changing it in Hostinger, update `SMTP_PASSWORD` in both `.env` files. With this fix, no PHP reload is needed for the new password to take effect.
- **17 players** who signed up since 24 October still aren't activated. Their emails never arrived, so they'd need to use the "resend" option on the activation page, or you could activate them in the admin panel.

<?php

namespace App\Filters;

use CodeIgniter\Filters\SecureHeaders as BaseSecureHeaders;

/**
 * CodeIgniter's secure headers, with the browser-default Referrer-Policy instead of "same-origin".
 * "same-origin" strips the page address from requests to Google's ad servers, which AdSense
 * needs; "strict-origin-when-cross-origin" still never sends paths or query strings off-site.
 */
class SecureHeaders extends BaseSecureHeaders
{
    protected $headers = [
        'X-Frame-Options' => 'SAMEORIGIN',
        'X-Content-Type-Options' => 'nosniff',
        'X-Download-Options' => 'noopen',
        'X-Permitted-Cross-Domain-Policies' => 'none',
        'Referrer-Policy' => 'strict-origin-when-cross-origin',
    ];
}

content.text:
The site was already mostly set up for AdSense. I fixed the four gaps I found; they're on staging, not production, and nothing is committed yet.

**Already in place:**
- `ads.txt` with your publisher ID (pub-5636695863753930).
- The AdSense script and Google's own consent message, which covers Europe, the UK and Switzerland.
- Google Consent Mode v2, set to "denied" until a visitor agrees.
- Privacy and cookie policies that cover AdSense, Google's ad cookies and the opt-out link.
- About, contact, terms and disclaimer pages, and a sitemap of the public pages.

**What I changed:**
1. **No ads on pages without content.** AdSense policy bans ads on sign-in, sign-up and similar screens, so the ad script now skips the login, register, sign-in link, activation, demo-save and complete-profile pages, and the "this feature is locked" page. Any page can also opt out with a `no_ads` section.
2. **Referrer header.** CodeIgniter's security-headers filter sent `Referrer-Policy: same-origin`, which hides the page address from Google's ad servers. A small subclass, `app/Filters/SecureHeaders.php`, now sends `strict-origin-when-cross-origin`. This also ends production's two conflicting referrer headers.
3. **robots.txt.** Google's ad crawlers (`Mediapartners-Google`, `AdsBot-Google`) may now read every page. Before, they inherited the game-page blocks meant for search engines.
4. **One consent pop-up in Europe.** Where Google's consent message runs, the site's own cookie banner now stays hidden instead of asking a second time. Elsewhere it shows as before, or after 2 seconds if Google's tool doesn't answer.

**Tested on staging:**
- **Ad script:** present on the home, about, FAQ, updates and privacy pages; absent on login, register and the sign-in-link page.
- **Locked page:** rendered directly, it has no ad script, while a normal page does.
- **At the server:** bypassing Cloudflare, it sends the new referrer header and serves the new robots.txt.

**Not tested:** the single-pop-up behaviour in Europe. Google only shows its consent message to European visitors, and my tests come from the US.

**Two things only you can do, both in the Cloudflare dashboard:**
- **Referrer header:** Cloudflare overrides it back to `same-origin`, which matches its "Add security headers" option. Turn that off under Rules → Transform Rules → Managed Transforms.
- **robots.txt:** Cloudflare caches it for 4 hours. Purge it after the production deploy so Google sees the new version right away.

**One risk for approval:** AdSense reviewers judge the public content, and the public side of the site is small (home, about, FAQ, updates, roadmap); the leaderboard and the game itself need a login. Making the leaderboard viewable without an account would add useful public content.

content.text:
The AdSense changes are live on production and pushed to Entire and GitHub as commit `6a02ccf` on `main`.

- **Backup:** the previous versions of the changed files are in `/root/prod-adsense-backup-1793159820` on the VPS. No database data changed.
- **Ad script:** loads on the home, about, FAQ, updates and privacy pages, and not on login, register or the sign-in-link page. All of them load normally.
- **Referrer header:** the server now sends Google's recommended `strict-origin-when-cross-origin`; before, it sent two conflicting values.
- **robots.txt:** the server serves the new rule letting Google's ad crawlers read every page.
- **Errors:** none since the deploy.

Two Cloudflare dashboard changes are still needed:
1. **Referrer header:** turn off "Add security headers" under Rules → Transform Rules → Managed Transforms. Cloudflare still replaces the header with `same-origin` before visitors receive it.
2. **robots.txt:** purge it from the cache. Otherwise Cloudflare keeps serving the old copy for up to 4 more hours.

After those, the site is ready to submit for AdSense review. Making the leaderboard public would strengthen the application, because the public content is still small.

- browseros-neo: The user's dedicated browser for agents — a real browser signed into their accounts, with live logins and a persistent profile. Use it for any task that touches a website or browser (open, read, act, fill, sign in, download, verify). The user installed it precisely so agents default here unprompted — over in-app browser tools, devtools/playwright automation, or headless fetching. When the user says "use neo", "use browserclaw", "use BrowserOS", or "use BrowserOS neo", use BrowserOS neo over MCP.
- refrax-ctl: Browse the web, fetch pages, and automate browser interactions via Refrax. Use this skill whenever the user's task involves fetching web content, reading web pages, researching topics online, opening URLs, taking screenshots of websites, filling out web forms, managing browser tabs, or any web-related task — even if they don't mention "browser" or "Refrax" explicitly. If a task requires accessing a URL or interacting with a web page, this skill applies. Refrax auto-launches if not running. Do NOT use for general macOS automation unrelated to the web.
- sentry:sentry-create-alert: Create Sentry alerts using the workflow engine API. Use when asked to create alerts, set up notifications, configure issue priority alerts, or build workflow automations. Supports email, Slack, PagerDuty, Discord, and other notification actions.
- sentry:sentry-debug-issue: Debug and fix a Sentry issue — find it (by link, ID, or search), pull full context (stack trace, breadcrumbs, trace, logs), optionally run Seer root-cause / autofix, apply the code fix, and resolve it via a `Fixes PROJECT-NAME-12A` commit/PR. Use when working a known error or hunting one down to fix.
- sentry:sentry-fix-stack-traces: Make Sentry stack traces readable — upload source maps for JavaScript/TypeScript, or debug files for native and mobile (dSYM, ProGuard/R8, NDK symbols, Dart obfuscation maps, .NET PDBs). Use when frames in Sentry show minified names, bundled paths, hex addresses, "unknown", or method names with no file/line, instead of your original source.
- sentry:sentry-get-started: Guided entry point for using Sentry through your agent. Orients you to your current setup and, for a new project, sets up Sentry end to end with sane defaults — provision a project, install the SDK (errors, tracing, and whatever it enables by default), and confirm real telemetry reaches Sentry. Routes other intents (adding more signals, fixing issues) to the right skill.
- sentry:sentry-instrument: Instrument an application with Sentry — detect the platform, install and initialize the SDK if needed, and wire up any signal — error monitoring, tracing/performance, logging, metrics, profiling, session replay, user feedback, cron check-ins, and AI/LLM monitoring (agent runs, token cost, and conversations for OpenAI, Anthropic, Vercel AI, LangChain, Google GenAI, Pydantic AI, and Laravel AI). Use to add Sentry to a project or to capture more than errors.
- sentry:sentry-otel-exporter-setup: Configure the OpenTelemetry Collector with Sentry Exporter for multi-project routing and automatic project creation. Use when setting up OTel with Sentry, configuring collector pipelines for traces and logs, or routing telemetry from multiple services to Sentry projects.
- sentry:sentry-setup-releases: Set up Sentry releases and deploy tracking — tag events with a version and environment, create the release in CI with its commits, and wire up suspect commits and code mappings, so Sentry can show which release introduced an issue, which commit is responsible, and release health. Use when asked to set up releases, track deploys, see what changed, or when issues show an unknown release or no suspect commit.
- sentry:sentry-snapshots-cocoa: Full Sentry Snapshots setup for Apple/Cocoa projects. Use when asked to "setup SnapshotPreviews", "setup Apple snapshot testing", "upload Apple snapshots to Sentry", "setup Apple snapshot GitHub Actions", or "setup Apple selective snapshot testing".

content.text:
The improved /staff/hire page is on staging and tested. It isn't on production or committed yet.

**What was wrong:**
- **Vague or wrong role descriptions.** The manager badge promised "+5% efficiency", and nothing said what each role really does.
- **No sense of usefulness.** You could hire a chef with no restaurant or a third mechanic, even though one mechanic covers every lift. Those people just cost a salary, lose morale, and eventually quit.
- **Idle new hires.** New staff arrived unassigned and did nothing until you used auto-assign on the staff page.
- **Misleading Hire button.** It only checked whether you could afford one day's salary, as if that were the price; there's no hiring fee.

**What the page does now:**
- Each role shows what it really does in the game, taken from the nightly game tick (for example "+3% skiers each, and up to 10 ski lessons a day at 50 €").
- It shows the real daily salary after your difficulty's cost multiplier.
- It shows how many you have, how many are working, and how many posts exist.
- Each role gets a verdict: **Needed**, **Useful**, **Enough for now** or **No post yet**, with the reason. A banner at the top lists what's needed.
- New hires go straight onto the first free post for their role, and the message says where. If there's no post, it warns they'll lose morale.
- After hiring you stay on the hire page, so hiring several is quicker.

**Tested on staging** with a fresh test account (#107: a lift, a slope, a restaurant, an unmanned groomer, an idle instructor, a working mechanic):

| Role | Verdict shown |
|---|---|
| Groomer Operator | Needed (the groomer had no driver) |
| Chef | Needed (the restaurant had none) |
| Lift Mechanic | Enough for now (one covers every lift) |
| Instructor | Enough for now (one already idle) |
| Resort Manager | Useful |
| Ski Patrol | Useful |
| Medic, Snowmaker, Park Crew, Receptionist | No post yet |

- **Hiring:** the groomer operator, chef and ski patrol each landed on the right post, an invalid role was refused, and the verdicts flipped to "Enough" afterwards.
- **Payroll:** 5,460 €/day, matching the five salaries.
- **Errors:** the only new log entries are bots probing for files.

**CSS build is broken locally.** The new commits on `main` (terrain parks, Sentry) changed `package.json`, but `npm install` wasn't run, so `npm run build` fails here. I avoided needing a rebuild by using classes both stylesheets already have, and I didn't upload any CSS, because staging has a newer stylesheet from that other work. Run this before the next CSS change:

```bash
npm install
```

content.text:
The redesigned hire page is on staging and tested at desktop and phone widths. It isn't on production or committed yet. The gameplay rules are the same as before.

**New layout:**
- **Header:** cash, staff count and total salaries per day, side by side.
- **"Your resort needs" panel first:** each needed role on one line with the reason ("Your groomer has no driver.", "1 restaurant has none."), its salary, and a Hire button right there. When nothing is needed, it says so and points to roles that would still help.
- **Filter tabs:** All, Worth hiring, Slopes & lifts, Guests & buildings. On phones the tab bar scrolls by itself.
- **Compact role cards:** what the role does, the verdict and its reason, then salary, how many you have (and how many are working) and the number of posts next to the Hire button. Roles that wouldn't help have a faded icon and a plain button.

**Tested on staging** with a fresh test account (#108):
- **Needs panel:** it listed Groomer Operator and Chef.
- **Filters:** each tab showed exactly the right roles.
- **One-click hire:** hiring from the panel put the new groomer operator on the groomer, and the panel then listed only Chef.
- **Phone width:** no sideways scrolling.

Testing turned up two problems, both fixed:
- The wording "1 of your 1 groomers has no driver" now reads "Your groomer has no driver."
- The last filter tab was cut off on phones; the tab bar now scrolls instead.

The work is in a temporary copy of the repo based on `main`, so your checkout on `feature/enhance-terrain-parks` is untouched. I used only classes the live stylesheet already has, because the local CSS build still needs `npm install`.
